name: Collagen Type III Glomerulopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Collagen Type III Glomerulopathy

criteria.description: Presence of type III collagen deposits in the mesangium and subendothelial space on renal biopsy
Electron microscopy showing characteristic fibrillar collagen bundles within glomerular capillary walls and mesangium
Proteinuria and nephrotic syndrome with or without hypertension
Exclusion of other causes of glomerulopathy such as amyloidosis or fibrillary glomerulonephritis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of type III collagen deposits plus compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on renal biopsy with electron microscopy and immunohistochemical staining.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mesangial and subendothelial type III collagen deposition
pathognomonic.notes: Identified via renal biopsy and electron microscopy
searchTerms: type III collagen deposits in kidney

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: fatigue linked to chronic kidney failure
low energy due to kidney problems
high blood pressure from kidney disease

rare.symptomName: Extrarenal type III collagen deposition manifestations
rare.notes: Rare involvement of other organs reported
searchTerms: type III collagen buildup in other tissues

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal or mildly increased echogenicity
Electron microscopy revealing type III collagen fibrils in glomeruli
genetic: No specific gene mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
Possible familial clustering reported but genetic basis unclear
other: Immunohistochemical staining positive for type III collagen in glomerular deposits
Exclusion of amyloid and fibrillary glomerulonephritis by Congo red and immunofluorescence

distinguishingFeatures: Different fibril ultrastructure on electron microscopy
Fibrils larger than amyloid but distinct from type III collagen
Absence of type III collagen deposits

redFlags: Rapidly progressive proteinuria with declining renal function
Nephrotic syndrome unresponsive to standard therapy
Histopathological evidence of type III collagen deposits on renal biopsy
references: Ronco P, et al. Collagen type III glomerulopathy: a rare cause of nephrotic syndrome. Kidney Int. 2019.
Fogo AB. Collagenofibrotic glomerulopathy: a review. Kidney Int. 2015.
